title: How well does Meshy ai convert 2d drawings into 3d models?
author: No-Average9599
selftext: Hey guys, I'm looking for ways to streamline my game dev process. Would Meshy be good for this purpose or is there another ai tool that would be better? Thank you.

comments.author: sumane12
comments.body:
Most AI tools like meshy, hunyuan and trellis are getting good now, but i dont thing there is a high quality automated workflow.

Imo, the best way to get production ready assets is to split your 2d generation into individual peices, feet, legs, torso, head, arms, hands. Then generate those individual peices. Put them together in blender or something, then retopo the entire mesh, making sure to fix any issues/holes/textures along the way. Then animate the entire rig.

This is a good way to maximise efficiency, but also make sure your generations are not junk.

comments.author: MakanLagiDud3
comments.body: I would say decent. Too bad they charge a quota for it. There are workarounds but they're tedious.

comments.author: ScienceAlien
comments.body: Use nano to turn the drawings into realistic art first?

comments.author: PhotojournalistBig53
comments.body:
It does what it says. Lot of texture noise so not suitable for zoomed in shots but for isometric views it’s not bad. Only rigs bipedal humanoids though and doesn’t put bones in hands/fingers so for a middle of the road decent rigged model you need to take it to something like Accurig and rig the hands and possibly clean the model up in Blender if need be. 

It’s pretty constrained for clothes and hair. If you got long hair or dresses it doesn’t work at all. Only really works well with a-pose head on bipeds.

I’m using it for alpha state but will probably change to individually rendered bodyparts eventually.

comments.author: OldGoldCode
comments.body: They've trapped a bunch of tiny art goblins inside of an igloo in the domestic south pole and they poke them with a stick and shake pennies whenever you give a prompt. It's why there is a delay before it returns the result.

comments.author: CycleMother2006
comments.body: Huanyan 3d might still be doing 20 free credits a day that you could use to test with. I found it to be higher quality than Meshy and might give you a good idea of what to expect. But I suggest you do some serious learning about 3d models in game design and what they actually need to look like (mesh wise) to be usable. Especially if being animated. And be prepared to temper your expectations under that guise. 3d Gen is phenomenal for 3d printing right now, but I'm still hand modeling everything because it'd take me longer to retop to low poly than to just model from scratch anyway. And I have no desire to compete with AAA Game Studios on the realistic art front.

comments.author: DatabaseConstant7870
comments.body: Tripo does really well I find it to be more useful

comments.author: ecuaffecto
comments.body: It's keeps getting better, I can now provide multi viewpoint of a drawing and get a very acceptable 3d render for printing in a few minutes. I signed, of course, for the pro plan to get this but it was free so I tried it out, they ended up charging me for the full year on the day I tried to cancel, but their customer service was good and reversed the charge and were nice about it, so make sure to cancel earlier if u do.
